title: Lesson 17 · Syntax & Letter-Writing
blurb: The case rules, the agreement rules, and the parts of a friendly letter.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun or pronoun in ( )?

“Boys skate.” (boys)
items.explain: “boys” is the subject — nominative case.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun or pronoun in ( )?

“We ran over the bridge.” (bridge)
items.explain: “bridge” is the object of the preposition “over” — objective case.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun or pronoun in ( )?

“John’s hat is new.” (John’s)
items.explain: “John’s” shows ownership — possessive case.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun or pronoun in ( )?

“They saw us.” (us)
items.explain: “us” is the object of “saw” — objective case.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun or pronoun in ( )?

“Horses are animals.” (animals)
items.explain: “animals” is a predicate noun after “are” — nominative case.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun or pronoun in ( )?

“The dog’s bone is buried.” (dog’s)
items.explain: “dog’s” shows ownership — possessive case.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun or pronoun in ( )?

“Farmers plant corn.” (corn)
items.explain: “corn” is the object of “plant” — objective case.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun or pronoun in ( )?

“Birds fly south.” (Birds)
items.explain: “Birds” is the subject — nominative case.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“He ___ fast.”
items.explain: A singular subject takes a singular verb: he runs.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“Tom and Sue ___ here.”
items.explain: Two subjects joined by “and” take a plural verb: are.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“The dogs ___.”
items.explain: A plural subject takes a plural verb: the dogs bark.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“She ___ letters.”
items.explain: A singular subject takes a singular verb: she writes.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“The boys ___ late.”
items.explain: A plural subject takes a plural verb: the boys were.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“Neither book ___ mine.”
items.explain: “Neither” is singular: neither book is mine.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“You ___ right.”
items.explain: “You” takes “are”: you are right.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“The cat ___ milk.”
items.explain: A singular subject takes a singular verb: the cat drinks.

items.prompt:
Which part of a letter is this?

“May 1, 2026”
items.explain: The date belongs in the heading, at the top.

items.prompt:
Which part of a letter is this?

“Dear Grandma,”
items.explain: It names whom you write to — the greeting.

items.prompt:
Which part of a letter is this?

“I hope you are well and happy.”
items.explain: It is the message itself — the body.

items.prompt:
Which part of a letter is this?

“Yours truly,”
items.explain: It ends the letter politely — the closing.

items.prompt:
Which part of a letter is this?

“Henry” (at the bottom)
items.explain: The writer’s name at the bottom is the signature.

items.prompt:
Which part of a letter is this?

“Boston, Massachusetts” (at the top)
items.explain: The town at the top belongs in the heading.

items.prompt: Syntax is the part of grammar that treats what?
items.explain: Syntax treats the construction of sentences.

items.prompt: A subject is in which case?
items.explain: A subject is in the nominative case.

items.prompt: The object of a verb or preposition is in which case?
items.explain: An object is in the objective case.

items.prompt: Two singular subjects joined by “and” take which verb?
items.explain: Two subjects joined by “and” take a plural verb.

items.prompt: A pronoun agrees with its antecedent in what?
items.explain: A pronoun agrees with its antecedent in gender, person, and number.

items.prompt: Where does the date go in a letter?
options: In the heading, at the top
items.explain: The date goes in the heading, at the top.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun or pronoun in ( )?

“The queen rules.” (queen)
items.explain: “queen” is the subject — nominative case.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun or pronoun in ( )?

“They praised her.” (her)
items.explain: “her” is the object of “praised” — objective case.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun or pronoun in ( )?

“The child’s toy broke.” (child’s)
items.explain: “child’s” shows ownership — possessive case.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun or pronoun in ( )?

“Ships sail the sea.” (Ships)
items.explain: “Ships” is the subject — nominative case.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“Books ___ on the shelf.”
items.explain: A plural subject takes a plural verb: books are.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“Each boy ___ a seat.”
items.explain: “Each” is singular: each boy has a seat.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“My parents ___ home.”
items.explain: A plural subject takes a plural verb: my parents are.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“The baby ___ asleep.”
items.explain: A singular subject takes a singular verb: the baby is.

items.prompt:
Which part of a letter is this?

“Sincerely,”
items.explain: It ends the letter politely — the closing.

items.prompt:
Which part of a letter is this?

“Please write back soon.”
items.explain: It is part of the message — the body.

items.prompt:
Which part of a letter is this?

“Ann” (signed at the end)
items.explain: The writer’s name at the end is the signature.

items.prompt: A noun showing ownership is in which case?
items.explain: Ownership is shown by the possessive case.

items.prompt: An adjective belongs to (modifies) what?
items.explain: An adjective belongs to some noun or pronoun.

items.prompt: Which part of a letter comes first?
items.explain: The heading (town and date) comes first, at the top.
